newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing share market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing share market report.

text.p: Dutch blue chips ended almost one percent higher on Friday, recouping almost all of the previous day's losses in a session dominated by U.S. interest rate worries.
The AEX index ended up 6.32 points or 0.90 percent at 708.43, within a whisker of Wednesday's 708.55 close.
Dealers said an initial gain of some two points had been encouraged by firmer guilder bonds and a relatively limited decline on Wall Street.
The index held firm throughout, but dealers said trade was virtually non-existent ahead of key U.S. economic data.
Players regarded the figures as key pointers to the direction of U.S. interest rates, with the market extremely nervy about the prospect of another hike, dealers said.
"There was absolutely no volume early in the day," one said. "Players were mainly hanging back to await the U.S. data, although there were a few bargain hunters about."
The numbers sparked a flurry of activity late in the session, with the AEX index seesawing in brisk trade.
"March unemployment was in line with expectations at 5.2 percent, although some had been hoping against hope it would stay unchanged at 5.3 percent," one dealer said.
Non-farm payrolls were a little lower than forecast, but average hourly wages were significantly higher than expected showing there was still tightness on the labour market, another said.
"Clearly the inflationary pressure is still there and the fear of an interest rate hike is very much present," he said.
The market had reacted very nervously with a spate of short covering by professional investors, dealers said.
The index picked up briefly to around 716 points, but quickly fell back once more.
Nearly all the AEX component stocks were swept along in the melee, with no real stories in the market to merit individual treatment.
ING, which on Thursday lost one guilder in the general market downturn despite reporting record 1996 profits, more than made good the shortfall.
Shares in the financial services group added 1.30 guilders to 70.60. ABN Amro closed up one guilder at 121.70, back from its session peak of 123.10.
Dealers said they had seen some stock-picking in recent laggards Nutricia and Oce van der Grinten.
